n1.text:
1 · KANJI, DECK ONLY
Borrows: Every character's 900×316 shell with Look it up's header and foot bar; the ink glyph tile and the vermilion 'not installed' line are screen-lookup.png's own; the hatched dash rows are The Exam's rule for an absence (screen-level.png); the ',' key and 'NOT INSTALLED · 6 MIN' chip are settings'.
Changed vs tools.html plate TWO: that plate re-cut the sheet (extra band, 280 body, new column widths). Here the shell and all three columns are identical to the dictionary state; the middle column stays and names what is missing, so the two states are one object and Escape, replay and column edges never move.
Data (tools.html's run for 語): N5 from the deck, Kanji N5 · Study & Language, tags kanji · n5, parts 言 口 五, no stroke count.

n2.text:
2 · KANJI, WITH THE DICTIONARY
Borrows: the same shell; compounds in the lookup's own row form.
Changed vs tools.html plate ONE: dropped the keys it invented (←→ column, ENTER searches a compound); '+ MORE' became a count the payload can give, '4 OF 12+' (12 compounds carried, has_more true); the part chips are Every character's chip, not a new one; only ENTER replays and ESC goes back.
Data is tools.html's run for 漢. Its N3 chip is the KANJIDIC level bug tools.html flagged (the deck files 漢 under N4); drawn as the code would show it.
Columns are 200 / 330 / 370 in both states.

n3.text:
3 · CONVERSATION, CHOOSING A LEVEL
Borrows: past-three's session sheet (322 | work cell), Scenes.tsx's scene copy (screen-scenes.png), and the round's slip and slab.
Changed vs tools.html plate THREE: the objectives moved into the prompt cell, so the scene reads whole on the left and the work cell holds only the choice; each level now carries the one real number that differs (AUDIO 0.85× vs 1×); the heading is English-led (TALK 会話, not 会話 TALK); the grading and privacy notes stay verbatim, small, under the choice. Level is ←→ and ENTER, not digits.

n4.text:
4 · CONVERSATION, ASKING
Borrows: past-three's round (the line is the specimen, the rule is the reply, the slab is the one hot thing).
Changed vs tools.html plate FOUR: the mic is paper while idle and turns vermilion only when recording, so SAY IT is the single hot object (tools.html had an ink mic beside a vermilion slab); two lines of invented copy are gone ('asking never counts as an attempt', '2 more on this line') since the crown already says HINT 1 OF 3; the hint slip is the hint's own ladder step. English stays shown; Ctrl+M speaks.

n5.text:
5 · CONVERSATION, ANSWERED
Borrows: past-three plate TWO (nothing moves; the correction is vermilion, the next thing is ink).
Changed vs tools.html plate FIVE: the heading mark turns vermilion on a partial, as the round's does on a miss; the invented explanatory sentence under the rule is removed (the mistake's authored explanation exists but only the Summary shows it today, so using it is Robbie's call); the correction and the barista's next line stay until ENTER. The model answer (YOU COULD ALSO SAY) still never appears here: it only arrives when attempts run out.

n6.text:
6 · CONVERSATION, FINISHED
Borrows: past-three's score block and objective rows; the draft panel's own fields (Front, Back, Reading, Notes) and actions.
Changed vs tools.html plate SIX: the FIX slip is gone (it was the fourth card's content twice); only the card under the cursor opens its four fields, the others are one line, so four ACCEPT/DISMISS pairs become one ACCEPT slab, the screen's one vermilion; '4 CARDS TO REVIEW' is the crown's owed chip; the score's /4 is gold, not vermilion; 'Show full transcript' and 'Replay scenario' are the panel's real actions. (A run left early would head this ENDED EARLY, the summary's other heading; not drawn.)

n6b.text:
6b · THE QUESTION AND THE FAILURE
The leave confirmation is the slab turned into its two answers (SCENARIO_COPY, split at the full stop). The failed save keeps the panel's own sentence; 'Try saving again' is the new slab Robbie asked for, and (…) is the reason the error carries.

diff.text:
WHAT THIS CHANGES FROM tools.html (plates 1–6)
Across all six: English leads the heading (TALK 会話); the scrim plates show the dimmed front-door chips and key hints, as screen-lookup.png does; every plate is on its section's real backdrop at 1280×720.
Kanji: same shell for both states (tools.html re-cut it for deck only); deck-only now leads; dropped invented keys; compound count not '+ MORE'.
Conversation: objectives moved to the prompt cell on the level screen; mic idle is paper; vermilion is only ever the one hot thing; invented sentences removed; the finished sheet has one ACCEPT slab and one open card instead of four button pairs; the score is gold.
Decided by Robbie, drawn here, not built: Ctrl+M, the correction held until Enter, 'Try saving again'. New and still his call: the ',' key on the deck-only sheet, one open card with a single ACCEPT slab, and where SKIP ALL sits.
